title: The Mystery of the Invisible Building Blocks
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about atomicity and valency — counting atoms in molecules and how atoms combine.

questions.prompt: What does atomicity tell us about a molecule?
choices: The total number of atoms in the molecule
The number of bonds an atom can form
questions.explanation: Atomicity is the total number of atoms present in one molecule.

questions.prompt: What is the atomicity of water, H₂O?
questions.explanation: Water (H₂O) has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom, so its atomicity is 3.

questions.prompt: According to the story, what is the common valency of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen’s common valency is 2 — its combining capacity.

questions.prompt: What is the atomicity of phosphorus, P₄?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus (P₄) has 4 atoms in one molecule, so its atomicity is 4.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly explains the difference between atomicity and valency?
choices: Atomicity counts atoms in a molecule, while valency describes an atom's combining capacity
Atomicity describes combining capacity, while valency counts atoms in a molecule
Atomicity and valency always have the same value
Atomicity and valency both describe the mass of atoms
questions.explanation: Atomicity counts the atoms in a molecule; valency describes an atom’s combining capacity.
